q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Cyclone Idai killed at least 157 people in Zimbabwe and Mozambique although it tore across Southern Africa.
solution:
The word 'although' is used to mean 'in spite of or even though'. This doesn't make sense in the context of this sentence as the killing of the people by the cyclone is a result of it tearing across South Africa, not despite it.

It would be better to rewrite the sentence as:

*Cyclone Idai killed at least 157 people in Zimbabwe and Mozambique as it tore across Southern Africa. *

Therefore, the part in option 3 has the error.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

We had to decline several orders in case that the production was held up due to labour strike.
solution:
The phrase 'in case' is used in situations where we talk about being prepared for something that may happen.

It acts as a conjunction between two clauses where one clause mentions a precaution and the second mentions a possibility.

Clause 1 + *in case *+ Clause 2

Constructions with 'in case' do not need the conjunction 'that' to join the two clauses. Therefore, the 'that' in the given sentence is unnecessary.

Hence, option 2 has the error.

The correct sentence is: *We had to decline several orders in case the production was held up due to labour strike. *

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

She got two quick promotions in order that she has good communication skills.
solution:
The correct answer is option 4.

*She got two quick promotions in order that she has good communication skills.*

In place of 'in order that' we should use 'because' to make the sentence correct as it means that she got promotions because of her communication skills.

So, options 1,2 and 3 are incorrect.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Due to the Cyclone Idai vast areas of land have been flooded, roads destroyed and communications disrupting in Zimbabwe and Mosambique.
options: vast areas of land have been flooded
solution:
The correct answer is option 4.

*Due to Cyclone Idai vast areas of land have been flooded, roads destroyed and communications disrupting in Zimbabwe and Mosambique*.

It can be clearly observed that the sentence is in past participle form from the words 'have been flooded, roads destroyed'.

So, we will use the past participle form of the verb 'disrupt' i.e 'disrupted'.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Torrential rains and winds of up to 170 km per hour swept away roads, homes, and bridges and knocking down power and communication lines.
solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

"Knocking down" which is in the present continuous tense should be changed to "knocked down" which is in the

simple past tense.

The other phrasal verb given in the sentence "swept away" is in simple past and the sentence would become grammatically incorrect if the other word is in present continuous.

The simple past tense is a verb tense that is used to talk about things that happened or existed before now.

The rest of the options are grammatically correct and shouldn't be changed.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

She lost a big order from a known showroom in case of her own carelessness.
solution:
The “in case of” part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect.

The correct phrase that should be used here is “due to”. It means “because of; owing to.”

Eg: "he had to withdraw due to a knee injury"

The person mentioned in the sentence given in the question lost a big order because of her own carelessness.

The phrase “in case of” means “in the event of (a particular situation).”

Eg: "instructions about what to do in case of fire"

Hence the correct answer is option 4.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Cyclone Idai is regarded as one of the worst tropical cyclone on record to affect Africa and the Southern Hemisphere as a whole.
solution:
The correct answer is the worst tropical cyclone

Key Points

• 'One of the worst tropical cyclones' should be there in place of 'One of the worst tropical cyclone'

• The 'one of' is a singular term and generally used to talk about a noun or a pronoun.

• The noun or a pronoun used after the phrase “one of” is always in the plural form.

• The helping verb will always be in the singular form, as the helping verb agrees with “one of” and not with the plural noun in the sentence.

Example: *One of the students was selected to visit NASA.*

Thus, the correct sentence is: *Cyclone Idai is regarded as one of the worst tropical cyclones on record to affect Africa and the Southern Hemisphere as a whole. *

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Every employee of the company were given a two-bedroom flat as a Diwali bonus.
solution:
Method:
1. Identify the subject of the sentence.
2. Check if the subject is singular or plural.
3. Match the subject with the correct verb form (Subject-Verb Agreement).

Explanation:
The subject of the sentence is "Every employee". In English grammar, words like Every, Each, and Everyone are always considered singular. Since the subject is singular, the verb must also be singular. Therefore, "were given" (plural) must be replaced with "was given" (singular).

Why the others are wrong:
(A) as a Diwali bonus is grammatically correct as it functions as a prepositional phrase.
(B) a two-bedroom flat is correct as it uses a hyphenated compound adjective to describe the noun.
(C) Every employee is the correct subject form; the error lies in the verb that follows it.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

I know the cobbler which mends the shoes outside the gate of our colony.
solution:
We use relative pronouns such as 'who', 'which', 'that' etc. to join two clauses, based on the subject from the first clause that is being referred to in the second clause.

In the given sentence, the subject from the first clause is 'the cobbler'. Since the subject is a person, the relative pronoun we will use to join the two given clauses should be 'who', not 'which'.

The correct version of the given sentence will be: *I know the cobbler who mends the shoes outside the gate of our colony.*

Hence, we can see that the part of the sentence which has the error is in option 4.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The street artist Satish Munjal has been painting this wall since the past one week.
solution:
Let us look at the meaning of the given sentence. We can see that the sentence wants to convey that the artist has continued painting the wall over a period of one week.

The usage of the word 'since' is incorrect here because it is used to refer to the specific starting point of an action.

For example: *I have been waiting for him since 5 o'clock.*

*(*The action of waiting started at 5 o'clock and has been continuing till the present time).

The correct version of the sentence will be: *The street artist Satish Munjal has been painting this wall for the past one week.*

'For' is the preposition used to refer to the period it has taken since the starting point of an action till the present time.

Therefore, the part of the sentence in option 2 has the error.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The river Yamuna has many non-native species like goldfish that is affecting its ecosystem.
solution:
The correct answer is option 4.

*The river Yamuna has many non-native species like goldfish that is affecting its ecosystem.*

The subject i.e. 'species' is in plural form. So, we will use the plural form of the verb i.e 'are' instead of 'is' for subject-verb agreement.

The correct sentence is - *The river Yamuna has many non-native species like goldfish that are affecting its ecosystem.*

So, options 1,2 and 3 are incorrect.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

We will rest for some time when we will reach the top.
solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

*We will rest for some time when we will reach the top.*

When we use 'when' as a conjunction and refer to something in the future, we always use the present perfect or simple present tense in the when clause, and not 'will/shall'. In the given sentence, we have used 'when we will' which is incorrect. It should be 'when we reach' the top.

Also, two 'will's in a single conditional sentence are redundant.

So, options 2,3 and 4 are incorrect.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

She forgot lock the door when she went out in a hurry.
solution:
The --She forgot lock-- part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect.

The correct phrase that should be used here is ---She forgot to lock--. The infinitive form of the verb --lock-- should be used.

Basically, an infinitive verb is a verb with the word to in front of it.

•

to be

•

to have

•

to hold

•

to sleep

•

to dream

When you use an infinitive verb, --to--- is a part of the verb. It is not acting as a preposition in this case. And the verb is always just the verb. It's not conjugated in any way - no -ed, no -ing, no -s on the end.

There are several possible ways to use infinitive verbs. You can use them:

•

as the subject of a sentence - To err is human; to forgive, divine.

•

like an adjective or adverb phrase that expresses purpose or intent - My instructions are to press this button every hour.

•

following an indirect object - He told me to give this to you.

•

following certain other verbs:

•

afford - We can't afford to eat out every night.

•

agree - Let's agree to disagree.

•

aim - I aim to please.

Hence the correct answer is option 1.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Lodi Colony in Delhi is very different from other places in the city that is crowded and noisy.
solution:
The that is crowded and noisy part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect.

The correct phrase that should be used here is-- that are crowded and noisy. The Subject-Verb agreement rule is not followed here.

Subjects and verbs must AGREE with one another in number (singular or plural). Thus, if a subject is singular, its verb must also be singular; if a subject is a plural, its verb must also be plural. Other places is plural, hence the verb that follows it must also be plural- --are.

the correct sentence is- Lodi Colony in Delhi is very different from other places in the city that are crowded and noisy.

Hence the correct answer is option 2.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The Doon Valley with all its lights look beautiful at night from the top of the mountain.
solution:
Option 2 is the correct solution.

'look beautiful' contains grammatical error. It should be 'looks beautiful' its more appropriate.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The Japanese artist Yoh Nagao was busy splashing the wall from colours.
solution:
Option 4 is the correct answer.

Key Points

• The error lies in the last part of the sentence.

• 'from colours' is grammatically wrong.

• The preposition 'with' meaning 'using' is used to refer to what we use to do something.

• Example: *They opened the package with a knife.*

• According to the context of the given sentence, the artist is *using colors to splash the walls*, therefore, the correct preposition to be used here would be 'with'.

• Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.

Thus the sentence would read: *The Japanese artist Yoh Nagao was busy splashing the wall with colours.*

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Each of the girls have given an impressive dance performance.
solution:
The word 'each' is always used to refer to a single individual. Even as it is followed by a plural noun such as in the construction 'each of the girls', the subject of the sentence will remain singular.

Hence, the verb must also take its singular form.

Therefore, the correct form of the verb should be 'has', not 'have' and the correct sentence will be: *Each of the girls has given an impressive dance performance.*

Hence, the correct answer is option 1, since that is the part of the sentence with error.

q:
In the sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

If so many catches had not being dropped, we would have won the match.
solution:
The construction 'had being' is not a grammatical construction.

The given sentence can be made grammatical by correcting the verb form to denote that something happened in the past. This is represented by the past perfect tense i.e.* had* +* been* + past participle of verb.

Note that the verb 'be' in past perfect constructions is in its past participle form 'been' instead of its present continuous tense 'being'.

The correct sentence will be: *If so many catches had not been dropped, we would have won the match.*

Hence, option 4 is correct.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Most disputes can be solved amicably unless one are rigid.
solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

*Most disputes can be solved amicably unless one are rigid.*

The singular noun one does not agree with the plural verb are. Instead of are, it should be is. A singular noun requires a singular verb whereas a plural noun requires a plural verb for subject-verb agreement in a sentence.

The correct sentence is --*Most disputes can be solved amicably unless one is rigid.*

So, options 1,3 and 4 are incorrect.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

In the northern suburbs of Bengaluru, home to the bulk of the information technology industry, the water crisis is even worst.
solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

*In the northern suburbs of Bengaluru, home to the bulk of the information technology industry, the water crisis is even worse*

The third degree of the adjective is used when a thing is surpassing all others in property or effect whereas the second degree is used when we do a comparison. In the given sentence, second degree of adjective should be used i.e worse instead of worst because it is preceded by the word even which means that the speaker is making a comparison with another place.

So, options 2,3 and 4 are incorrect.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

No sooner did he see the tiger when he ran as fast as he could.
solution:
The construction no sooner...than is used to represent a situation in which the second event occurs immediately after the first.

For example:* No sooner had the teacher left the classroom than the children started to scream.*

The use of when in the given sentence is, therefore, incorrect.

Hence, the error is in the part of the sentence in option 1.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The match is about to begin since the captain as well as the team are on the field.
options: The match is about to begin
solution:
The construction as well as is used to conjoin two expressions, but it cannot be used in the way that we use and. It is used to add an expression with the first one but not to combine them together.

For example, we say: '*My mother and father are coming to the party'. *(The subject becomes plural)

But when we use as well as we say: *'My mother, as well as my father, is coming to the party.' *(The subject my mother remains singular)

Therefore, in the given sentence, it is inaccurate to use the plural verb form are since the subject of the verb is the captain i.e. singular.

Hence, the error is in the part of the sentence in option 1.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Supriya asked Kiran that where had her mother gone when the results of the contest were being declared.
options: when the results of the contest
that where had her mother gone
solution:
Option 3 is the segment with the error

that where had her mother gone... is grammatically wrong. The correct formation would be -- Supriya asked Kiran where her mother had gone when the results of the contest were being declared.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

On the way he was bited on his toe by a venomous snake.
solution:
The correct answer is he was bited.

Key Points

• Option 3 is the segment with the error.

• he was bited is grammatically wrong because past participle of a bite is bitten.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

There isn't many rice left in the house so we must replenish our stock soon.
solution:
The word rice is an uncountable noun. Therefore, it is incorrect to quantify it with the adjective many.

It is instead correct to refer to a quantity of rice with adjectives used for non-countable nouns, such as much or a lot of.

In this sentence, it would be correct to say-- there isn't much rice left....

Therefore, the error is in option 4.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Ten kilometres are a long distance to cover on foot for a child.
solution:
Method:
1. Identify the subject of the sentence: "Ten kilometres".
2. Check if the subject represents a single unit or multiple individual items.
3. Apply the rule for units of measurement.
4. Replace the verb 'are' with 'is'.

Explanation:
When a plural noun represents a specific amount, distance, weight, or period of time treated as a single unit, it takes a singular verb. Here, "Ten kilometres" is a single unit of distance, so it must be followed by 'is' instead of 'are'.

Why the others are wrong:
(B) a long distance is correct as it describes the singular unit of measurement.
(C) for a child is a correct prepositional phrase indicating the person affected.
(D) to cover on foot is a correct infinitive phrase used to describe the action.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

My father dissuaded me to try for a job as he wanted me to pursue higher studies.
solution:
The correct answer is option 2, to try for a job

The preposition to should not be used here. From should be used with the word dissuade. After the preposition from + verb +ing should be used here.So from trying should be written.

The correct sentence should be: My father dissuaded me from trying for a job as he wanted me to pursue higher studies.

That is why option 2 is the answer.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The length of a male swallow's tail reveal his attractiveness for a female swallow.
solution:
The subject for the verb 'reveal' in the given sentence is the noun phrase 'length of a mail's tail', which is singular.

Hence, the verb must change its form to 'reveals' in order to agree with the singular subject.

The correct sentence should be:

*The length of a male swallow's tail reveals his attractiveness for a female swallow.*

Hence, the error is in the part mentioned in option 4.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

He is more smarter than his brother though he does not earn much money.
solution:
Method:
1. Identify the adjective used for comparison: smarter.
2. Check if there is a modifier before it: more.
3. Apply the rule of Double Comparatives.

Explanation:
The word smarter is already the comparative degree of the adjective 'smart'. In English grammar, you cannot use both 'more' and the '-er' suffix together for the same adjective. This error is known as a double comparative. The correct sentence should be: "He is smarter than his brother..."

Why the others are wrong:
(A) though he does not earn is a correct subordinate clause using the present simple tense.
(C) much money is correct as 'much' is used with uncountable nouns like 'money'.
(D) than his brother is the correct way to introduce the person being compared.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The child along with his parents were waiting for the programme to begin.
solution:
Option 2 is the correct solution.

It should be was waiting for the because here was refers to the subject child which is singular.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Not complying by any of the laws can land you into serious trouble.
solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

*Not complying by any of the laws can land you into serious trouble.*

By is used mostly to state proximity, purpose or method while with is used to state : together, involved, having, using, feeling, agreement, understanding. In the given statement, complying should be followed by with as the statement describes the action of agreement with laws.

So, options 1,3 and 4 are incorrect.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Raja Ravi Varma was one of the first artist who tried to create a style that was both modern and traditional.
options: to create a style that was
solution:
The correct answer is option 3.

*Raja Ravi Varma was one of the first artist who tried to create a style that was both modern and traditional.*

The singular noun artist is followed by the quantifier one of the which always requires a plural form of the verb. Instead of artist , it should be artists.

So, options 1,2 and 4 are incorrect.

q:
Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.

"Unless you did not do your homework you will be punished," said the teacher.
solution:
The correct answer is 'Unless you did not'.

Key Points

• "Unless" already introduces a condition negating the need for "not."

• Thus, in the given sentence "did not do" will be replaced with "do"

• Correct sentence- "Unless you do your homework you will be punished," said the teacher.

q:
Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.

The reduction in the cost of education due to an increase in subsidies offer by the government is also seen as a reason to get more educated.
options: The reduction in the cost of education
due to an increase in subsidies
is also seen as a reason
solution:
The correct answer is option 4.

The offer should be replaced by offered as the past participle form of the verb should be used in this sentence because the government has already performed that action i.e. increase in subsidies. So, option 4 is correct.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

There is many modes of travel to go to Agra but I prefer road travel.
solution:
The correct answer is option 3.

The word many is plural so we have to use the plural form of verb i.e. are instead of is. So, option 3 is correct.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Having just taking a heavy lunch, she was not ready to have any fruit.
solution:
The correct answer is 'taking a heavy lunch'.

Key Points

• In this part of the sentence, there is an error in the given part - 'taking a heavy lunch'.

• 'taking' should be replaced by 'taken'.

• The structure 'having taken' is a perfect participle which functions as an adverbial modifier of time.

• Hence, the correct sentence is- 'Having just taken a heavy lunch, she was not ready to have any fruit.'

Hence, the correct answer will be Option 3.

Important Points

• An adverbial modifier is a word or phrase that modifies another part of a sentence, typically a verb or adjective.

• Adverbs of time tell us when an action happened, but also for how long, and how often. Adverbs of time are invariable.

• Soon now, later, then, tomorrow, today, day after tomorrow, everyday, weekly, annually, quarterly, yearly, yesterday, last month, tonight, last week, immediately, etc. are some examples of adverbs of time.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Cows are amongst the gentlest of animals; none shows more passionate tenderness towards their young ones.
solution:
The correct answer is "none shows more".

Key Points

• In the original sentence, "Cows are amongst the gentlest of animals; none shows more passionate tenderness towards their young ones," the error lies within how the subject and verb in the second part ("none shows more passionate tenderness towards their young ones") are paired.

• Let's break it down for clarity:

• The subject in the first part of the sentence is "Cows," which is plural.

• The phrase "none shows more passionate tenderness towards their young ones" refers back to "Cows."

• The pronoun "none" can be singular or plural depending on the noun it refers to.

• Since it refers to "Cows" (plural), "none" functions as a plural pronoun in this context.

• The verb "shows" is singular, which does not match the plural context indicated by the pronoun "none."

• Therefore, to correct the grammatical error, the singular verb "shows" should be changed to the plural form "show" to match the plural subject.

• So the correct sentence is: "Cows are amongst the gentlest of animals; none show more passionate tenderness towards their young ones."

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 3".

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The cost of fruits and vegetables have risen abnormally this month.
solution:
The correct answer is have risen

Key Points

• 'has risen' should be there in place of 'have risen'

• Usually, we match the verb with the nearest subject but this is wrong. Match the verb with the main subject of the sentence.

• Example:

• ​*The quality of apples is good.*

Thus, the correct sentence is: *The cost of fruits and vegetables has risen abnormally this month.*

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

You may left the class when you have completed the test.
solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

The sentence is clearly talking about an action that may occur in the future. Left is the past tense form of the verb which is incorrect. The correction would be leave. So, option 1 is correct.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Although there are more than a hundred known elements, they rarely occur at a pure state.
solution:
The correct answer is option 3.

Option 3 has an error. Instead of at, in is more appropriate because we are talking about the state in which they exist.

At is mostly used for a particular time or event. So, option 3 is correct.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Entering the hall, the show had started.
solution:
The correct answer is option 3.

Entering is in present continuous tense but the phrase had started is in past participle tense. So, option 3 contains an error. It should be --When I entered.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

"I done a lot of work today," she said.
solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

The given part is missing the verb have which makes the sentence incorrect. Therefore, option 1 is correct.-- It should be -- "I have done a lot of work today," she said.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Friction reduce the efficiency of machines so their value also gets reduced.
solution:
The correct answer is Friction reduce

Key Points

• 'Friction reduces' should be there in place of 'Friction reduce'

• The subject and verb must agree with each other in a sentence. When the subject is singular, the verb used should be singular, and when the subject is plural, the verb used should be plural.

• Also with uncountable nouns, a singular verb is used.

• Examples:

• *This news is very important.*

• *Your luggage looks heavy.*

• 'Friction' is an uncountable noun. So singular verb should be used.

• Thus, the correct sentence is: *Friction reduces the efficiency of machines so their value also gets reduced.*

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

I am sure that neither Juhi nor Jaya are responsible for breaking the vase.
solution:
Method:
1. Identify the subject of the sentence.
2. Check the conjunction used: neither...nor.
3. Apply the Rule of Proximity to the verb.
4. Replace the plural verb with a singular verb if the nearest subject is singular.

Explanation:
When two singular subjects are joined by neither...nor or either...or, the verb must agree with the nearest subject. Here, the nearest subject is "Jaya," which is a singular noun. Therefore, the plural verb "are" is incorrect and must be replaced by the singular verb "is".

Why the others are wrong:
(A) for breaking the vase is a correct prepositional phrase.
(B) neither Juhi nor Jaya is the correct way to use the correlative conjunction.
(C) I am sure that is a grammatically correct introductory clause.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

One of the boys from our school have been selected for National Badminton Championship
solution:
The correct answer is have been selected

Key Points

• 'has been selected' should be there in place of 'have been selected'

• The 'one of' is a singular term and generally used to talk about a noun or a pronoun.

• The noun or a pronoun used after the phrase “one of” is always in the plural form.

• The helping verb will always be in the singular form, as the helping verb agrees with “one of” and not with the plural noun in the sentence.

Example: *One of the students was selected to visit NASA.*

• Thus, the correct sentence is: *One of the boys from our school has been selected for National Badminton Championship*

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

I can swim very fast when I was only five.
solution:
The correct answer is I can swim

Key Points

• 'I could swim' should be there in place of 'I can swim'

• We use *can* and *can't* to talk about the ability to do something at a specific time in the present or future.

Example: *I can see you.

Help! I can't breathe.*

•

We use *could* and *couldn't* to talk about the past:

Examples: *She could speak several languages.

They couldn't dance very well.*

•

Since we are talking about past ability, we will use 'could'.

Thus, the correct sentence is:* I could swim very fast when I was only five.*

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The modern man is busy acquiring more and more wealth and designing ways to invest it in more sense pleasures.
solution:
The correct answer is option "2"

• The original sentence refers to the modern man acquiring more wealth in order to invest in pleasures, thus the term 'pleasures' acting as a noun should have an adjective before that describes it. This would be the adjective form of the verb 'sense', thus it would be 'sensory'.

• Correct Sentence :- The modern man is busy acquiring more and more wealth and designing ways to invest it in more sensory pleasures.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The Prime Minister, along with the other ministers have left for America.
solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. have left

As a rule, when a sentence refers to 2 subjects, the verbs in the sentence should refer to the subject that comes first. Here it is 'the Prime Minister' and he is a singular entity, thus the verbs should also be singular. Thus, 'have' needs to be replaced with 'has'.

Thus, the correct answer is option 1.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Deepa walked down the road slowly without looking anybody.
solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e looking anybody

The sentence is missing the preposition 'at' after the verb. One cannot walk down a road without 'looking anybody', one has to do that without 'looking at anybody' because 'looking' is an action that is done 'at' something.

Thus, the correct answer is option 3.

q:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Everything that I like to eat are fattening.
solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. are fattening

The sentence refers to 'everything I like to eat', while this refers to all food, the term 'everything' is a single entity and thus should be treated as such. The verb used to refer to this should also be singular and so 'are' needs to be replaced with 'is'.

q:

solution:

q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If there is no error, select ‘No error’.

They have lived / in this apartment / since ten years.
solution:
Method:
1. Identify the time expression: "ten years".
2. Check if the time is a point or a duration.
3. Apply the rule: Since is for a point in time; For is for a duration.
4. Replace "since" with "for" to see if it fits.

Explanation:
The error lies in the preposition used with the time period. Since is used for a specific starting point (e.g., 2010, Monday, 9 AM), whereas For is used for a period or duration of time (e.g., ten years, two hours, five months). Since "ten years" is a duration, we must use for.

Why the others are wrong:

(C) in this apartment is a correct prepositional phrase indicating location.
(D) They have lived is the correct use of the Present Perfect tense to show an action continuing from the past.

solution:

Explanation:
The error is in the verb tense and voice. The sentence intends to show that the construction is the cause of the population rise. "Is led to" is a passive construction that makes no sense here. Why the others are wrong:

q:
Directions: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

He win / several accolades / for his / music compositions.
solution:
Method:
1. Identify the subject: He (Third-person singular).
2. Identify the tense: The sentence describes a completed action or a general fact.
3. Check Subject-Verb Agreement: A singular subject requires a singular verb.
4. Correct the error: Change win to wins (Present Tense) or won (Past Tense).

Explanation:
The error lies in the subject-verb agreement. In English grammar, when the subject is He, She, It, or a singular noun, the verb in the Simple Present Tense must end with -s or -es. Since "He" is a singular subject, "win" is grammatically incorrect.

Why the others are wrong:
(A) several accolades is correct as 'several' is used with plural countable nouns.
(B) music compositions is correct as it uses a noun adjunct to describe the type of compositions.
(C) for his is a correct prepositional phrase showing possession.

q:

solution:

• ​Correct sentence: *The food in the new eatery is much better than the one in RK Puram.*

Additional Information

• When two items/people are compared, a comparative degree is used by putting ‘er’ to the adjective word in association with the word ‘than’.

• In some cases ‘more’ is used.

• Example: *She is smarter than her sister.

She is more cheerful than her sister.*

• Noun (subject) + verb + much + comparative adjective + than + noun (object).

•

q:

q:

5. Check for subject-verb agreement and grammatical errors.

q:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I find that/ I get myself tired/ very easily/ these days.
solution:
Method:
1. Read the sentence to check for logical flow and subject-verb-object consistency.
2. Check if the reflexive pronoun 'myself' is used correctly or if it is redundant.
3. Identify if the verb 'get' requires a reflexive pronoun in this context.

The error lies in the redundant use of the reflexive pronoun 'myself'. In English, we say "I get tired" to describe a state or condition. (C) these days is a correct time expression used for current trends.

q:
Directions: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

• The use of 'at' is grammatically incorrect.

• The preposition ‘at’ must be replaced with ‘to’.

q:

q: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of adverb of manner.

• Carefully is used as an adverb of manner.

• Thus, the sentence with the appropriate use of adverb of manner is option 3.

q:

• Replace the preposition "for" with "to" to correct the sentence.

• To is used to indicate the direction or destination of a particular place or something.

• Example - *We're going to Liverpool next week.*

• In the given sentence "to" should be used because a destination place is mentioned, that is the "town library."

• 'Which' is used after a preposition to represent a specified antecedent.

• The implied meaning of the sentence is: He used to respond by saying that the local library was the only location he visited.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 2, which contains an error.

q:

•

•

•

q:

• The word that must come after 'of' should be the object of the preposition 'of'. Hence, a gerund (working) must be placed after it.

q:

• The conjunction 'Unless' means except on the condition that or under any other circumstance than.

• So, we cannot use a negative word after 'unless' as it conveys a negative meaning itself.

• Also, 'goes' will be used as the subject is singular.

q:

solution:
The correct answer is the nurse were present. Key Points

• Was should be used instead of were.

• If a sentence has two subjects connected by or/nor, either/or, or neither/nor, the verb must agree with the second subject (the subject closer to the verb).

• *Example: Neither Rohan nor his friends were present at the party.*

• The helping verb should agree with the subject 'the nurse' (Singular) for the given sentence

• Therefore, a singular verb 'was' should be used instead of the plural verb 'were'.

• Thus, the option that contains a grammatical error is option 2.

q:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

They will go to bed / early since they / have to get up / at five on the morning.
solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: at five on the morning

Key Points

• The error here lies in the use of the preposition.

• Replace "on" with "in" to make the sentence correct.

• “In” and “on” are both time-based prepositions. We can use them in different ways when we want to talk about specific periods.

• We use in with morning, afternoon, evening and night when we are referring to a general time.

• For example- *I always work best in the morning.*

• But we use on when we talk about a specific morning, afternoon, etc., or when we describe the part of the day.

• For example- *On the morning of the 19th, I will have to rush to school.*

• The given sentence is talking about a general time in the morning, so the preposition "in" should be used here.

• Therefore, the correct answer is option 2, which contains the error in it.

q: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of prepositions.

It has been raining since morning.
solution:
Method:
1. Identify the tense: "has been raining" is Present Perfect Continuous.
2. Identify the time expression: "morning" is a point of time.
3. Apply the rule: Use since for a specific point of time and for for a duration.

Explanation:
In the Present Perfect Continuous tense, we use since to indicate the starting point of an action that began in the past and is still continuing. Since "morning" is a specific point in time, since is the only grammatically correct preposition here.

Why the others are wrong:
(A) Till indicates a deadline or end point, which doesn't fit the starting point context here.
(B) From is used for starting points in simple tenses, but in Perfect Continuous, we must use since.
(C) By is used to indicate "not later than" a certain time, which is incorrect here.

q:

q:

• Replace "from" with "to" in order to correct the sentence.

• From is used to refer to the place where someone or something starts or originates.

• To is used to indicate the person or thing that receives or experiences the object of the verb.

q:

• According to the rules of grammar, when an action is in progress at a certain time, we need to use 'continuous form of verb' after the conjunction 'while.'

q:

The newspaper reported / that it was a mystery / how the thieves enter / the house.

q:

• So, "got" should be used here in the given sentence.

• The preposition 'to' will be used instead of 'by' as it means in the direction of.

• Example: We went to Prague last year.

• We use "by + noun" to describe how someone travels or communicates, or how things are processed. (by car, by train etc.)

• Hence, the correct answer is option 3 which contains an error in it.

• The implied meaning of the sentence is: I had travelled to Kanpur on foot for the majority of the day before boarding the train to Mumbai.

q:

•

•

•

once you put the money in your

q:

q:

solution:

solution:
The erroneous part is: but to work hard.

Key Points

• 'no other' and 'than' are correlative conjunctions.

• Correlative conjunctions are pairs of words that work together to join two elements of equal importance within a sentence.

• In this case, "no other" and "than" are used as a correlative conjunction to express a comparison or contrast between two options.

• In the sentence, "no other" is used to emphasize that there are no alternative options available. It suggests that the person referred to in the sentence has exhausted all possibilities and has only one option left.

• "Than" is used to introduce the only remaining option, which is to work hard.

• The combination of "no other" and "than" acts as a correlative conjunction because they work together to join the elements of the sentence, indicating the limited choices and emphasizing the necessity to work hard.

• Hence, 'than' must replace 'but' to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *He knows that he has no other option than to work hard.*
